author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  the way the project records non-goal changes.

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction form opens on that visit's current values, is held to the booking rules, and updates the visit in place rather than adding a second one, then shows the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a description and a date later than today, when the correction is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown
given an accepted correction, when the pet's visits are counted, then the count is unchanged and no second visit exists
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then the correction is refused and the date is named
given a visit that is not the named pet's, when a correction is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit (NG-5)
a link or button on the owner detail page that opens the correction; the owner deferred the entry point to a possible follow-up request
changing which pet a visit belongs to; only the date and the description are correctable
new wording for the correction form or its confirmation
notes: Four open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md#open-questions rather than answered here, each taking the narrowest reading of the intake: no visible entry point, no new wording, no earlier-visits list on the correction form, and the future-date rule applying to corrections. The ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md needs a row for the new non-goal ADR; that file is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the create-and-edit shape PetController already shows in the owner package: one controller per entity carrying both handlers, and a shared form model attribute that branches on an optional path variable. PetController.findPet is the template — @PathVariable(name='petId', required=false) Integer, new Pet() when null, load through the owner when present. VisitController's @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit takes the same branch on visitId: present, it resolves the existing Visit from pet.getVisits() inside the loaded Owner; absent, it keeps creating and attaching a new one. No new package, pattern, dependency, or module boundary. One difference from PetController is load-bearing and saves work: PetController copies fields onto the existing pet because findPet loads its own Owner instance, while loadPetWithVisit puts the same Owner into the model that the correction handler binds — so binding onto the resolved Visit mutates the graph the handler saves, and update-in-place needs no copy step. docs/system-design.md § Contracts now carries REQ-VISITEDIT-001 on Owner, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController, and its invariant paragraph records that a visit under correction resolves only within the named pet's visits.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit join VisitController, reusing the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm view and the visit model attribute
the shared @ModelAttribute('visit') gains an optional visitId path variable; both booking handlers keep their current behavior unchanged
OwnerRepository.save stays the sole write path — the corrected Visit reaches the database by cascade from Owner, and no VisitRepository is introduced
the correction handler must not call owner.addVisit(petId, visit); that call is the only route to a second visit record

the shared template needs no edit: the heading drops 'New' for a persisted visit, the form posts to the current URL because it declares no action, and the Previous Visits row filter (th:if on the iterated visit) excludes only an unsaved visit — so the visit under correction is listed, which is the expected consequence of reusing the template
the future-date rule is currently inline in processNewVisitForm; both handlers holding one rule is a Refactor-step extraction into a private helper, not a new pattern

patterns.description: findPet — shared form model attribute branching on an optional id path variable to serve both the create and the edit handler; copy this shape for loadPetWithVisit
pet-not-found branch — IllegalArgumentException when the path identifier names nothing in the loaded owner's graph; the refusal for a visit that is not the named pet's takes the same form

@WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean OwnerRepository and an Owner-Pet fixture built in @BeforeEach; correction tests add a Visit with an id set to that pet, and the count assertion reads pet.getVisits() on the fixture after the POST

risks.risk: a visitId supplied by any unauthenticated caller could reach a visit belonging to another pet or owner
risks.mitigation: resolve the visit only from the named pet's visits inside the loaded Owner, never by identifier lookup against a repository; a miss refuses through the existing IllegalArgumentException branch. The @InitBinder already disallows id and *.id, so identity comes from the path alone

risks.risk: calling owner.addVisit on the correction path would add a second visit record
risks.mitigation: bind onto the resolved Visit and save the owner without adding; the count-unchanged acceptance criterion is the guard

risks.risk: binding mutates the live Visit, so a rejected correction redisplays the form with the submitted values echoed in the Previous Visits listing
risks.mitigation: accepted as-is. The PRD leaves the correction form's earlier-visits listing an open question; adding template branching for it would answer a question the owner deferred

risks.risk: a visit whose date has already passed cannot be saved with that date, because the future-date rule applies to corrections
risks.mitigation: accepted. PRD edge case 4 records exactly this; no carve-out and no separate past-visit path

risks.risk: minVisitDate renders a client-side min of tomorrow on the correction form, which a stale-dated visit will fail
risks.mitigation: display hint only. The server-side rejectValue check is authoritative; leave the fragment and the model attribute unchanged

notes: Narrowest readings taken where the PRD left a question open, per the dispatch: no visible entry point anywhere, no new wording (the button keeps #{addVisit} and the heading its shared form), no change to the earlier-visits listing, and the future-date rule applying unchanged to corrections. The javadoc on loadPetWithVisit was substantially expanded by this change (a new

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain status for this pass, so a human or CI can close it: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, org.springframework.boot 4.1.0, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native, cyclonedx 3.2.4, io.spring.javaformat), so dependencyCheckAnalyze was NOT run and no NVD matching happened in this review. Spring Boot resolves at 4.1.0 and the build declares no plain-HTTP repository. Treat the dependency set as not verified against the NVD rather than clean; the CycloneDX SBOM task is the natural hook for an external scan.

Non-blocking, and explicitly not a defect against the recorded baseline: processUpdateVisitForm binds the whole Owner aggregate via @ModelAttribute Owner owner and then saves it (VisitController.java:143,150), so request parameters naming owner fields or nested pet fields (for example firstName, telephone, pets[0].name) are persisted alongside the correction. This is identical to the pre-existing processNewVisitForm and to the wider controller shape, so the change is not weaker than the baseline in system-design.md#security-context and the mass-assignment row's control (the disallow list) is honoured. It is worth recording only because the new route widens an already-broad binding surface: a future narrowing would bind just the Visit and re-load the Owner for the save, closing it for both handlers at once.

The correction path sets no flash message while the booking path sets one (VisitController.java:134). Not a security concern, and the PRD's 'no new wording' non-goal explains it; noted only so a later reader does not read the asymmetry as an oversight.
approved_aspects: Access control on the new correction routes is sound: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit resolves the owner by path id, the pet only via owner.getPet(petId), and findVisit only from pet.getVisits() (VisitController.java:93-100). No repository lookup by visitId exists, so a visitId belonging to another pet or another owner is unreachable and refuses through the existing IllegalArgumentException branch. Basis: direct source read plus scripts/changeset.sh; the IDE oracle was not connected for this dispatch, so this is the weaker grep/read basis rather than a symbol-resolution citation. Both tests theVisitCorrection[Form]ShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotThePets cover the refusal.

Mass assignment: the existing @InitBinder disallowing 'id' and '*.id' (VisitController.java:51-54) is class-scoped and therefore already covers both new handlers. Identity comes from the path alone, so no form/URL identifier mismatch is possible on the correction path.

Fail secure on a rejected correction: binding mutates the live Visit inside the loaded Owner graph, but spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11) leaves that graph detached, and processUpdateVisitForm returns the form before owners.save on any binding error (VisitController.java:146-150). A refused correction therefore cannot reach the database by dirty checking. The design-block risk row anticipated only the echoed-values display effect; the persistence question also resolves clean.

Error-message disclosure: the new findVisit message interpolates only visitId and pet.getId(), both Integer-typed path variables, so a non-numeric value fails conversion before reaching the message. No request-derived text reaches the rendered error page, and the message carries no internal or sensitive detail. Same shape as the pre-existing pet-not-found message.

No new injection, file, process, deserialization, or template surface: the change adds no SQL, no Runtime/ProcessBuilder, no file I/O, no Jackson typing, and no template edit (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged, so Thymeleaf default escaping still covers the echoed description). Grep sweeps over src/main/java and src/main/resources/templates for the skill's detection patterns and for th:utext / __${...}__ returned nothing.
Concurrency: rejectDateNotInFuture is a stateless private helper and the controller singleton gains no mutable field.
No secrets added: a case-insensitive sweep of the added diff lines for password/secret/token/api-key/credential/private-key returned no hits.
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no dependency was added, removed, or re-versioned and the four new-dependency checks do not apply.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 ('Correcting a visit that is not the named pet's is refused, as booking against another owner's pet is') asks for cross-pet isolation, and the design-block's own risk list names it explicitly: 'a visitId supplied by any unauthenticated caller could reach a visit belonging to another pet or owner.' The two tests meant to cover this (theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotThePets, theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotThePets) use VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET = 2, but no second pet, owner, or visit with id 2 is ever created anywhere in the test fixture (@BeforeEach only builds one owner/pet/visit, all with id 1). The tests therefore exercise 'a visit id that does not exist at all' rather than 'a visit that belongs to a different pet' — the constant's name overstates what the test proves, and a regression that resolved visits by a global/cross-pet lookup instead of filtering pet.getVisits() would not be caught by either test.
findings.fix: Add a second Pet (optionally under a second Owner) carrying a real Visit with id VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET in the fixture, and assert the correction attempt against the first pet's URL for that id is refused. Rename the constant only if it continues to describe a genuinely different pet's visit.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction for a booked visit

blast_radius.note: One module and two code files. The new GET and POST edit routes are purely additive, and the one shared-path edit gives loadPetWithVisit an optional visitId that is null on both booking routes, so their behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged; no template, schema, build, config, or sensitive path is touched.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: rejectDateNotInFuture is the old inline check extracted verbatim, and the deliberate absence of owner.addVisit on the correction path is exactly what keeps the update in place, resting on loadPetWithVisit returning the Visit instance living inside the saved Owner. With open-in-view=false the graph is detached, so a rejected correction mutates only a throwaway object and save merges rather than inserts.

test_adequacy.note: Seven new MockMvc tests assert real post-state on the fixture, not just view names: the corrected visit's id, date, and description, and a visit count still at one, so a regression that booked a second visit would fail. The cross-pet isolation tests name a visit that genuinely exists on a sibling pet, so a globally-resolving lookup would be caught.

reviewer_hedging.note: Two of four round-2 approvals carry recommendations. The security reviewer records that processUpdateVisitForm binds and saves the whole Owner aggregate through the Owner model attribute, mass-assignment left unaddressed by design and matching booking, plus a dependency set never checked against the NVD; the doc reviewer records a self-created vocabulary inconsistency deferred out of slice.

scope_deviation.note: Zero consultations, zero build retries, and the single design revision was a vocabulary and doc-index reconciliation that re-decided nothing. The six doc files are the owner's explicit instruction to record the NG-5 narrowing, the deferred entry-point link stayed out, and the shared template listed as a file target was correctly left untouched.

rationale: The code is contained and the in-place mechanism is sound on a close read. Attention is owed to the reviewer residue, not the diff: the new POST route replicates the existing whole-Owner mass-assignment binding, knowingly. Note too that the future-date rule makes a past visit's description uncorrectable.
